## pointing_pointer.kt { #pointing-pointer-kt }

A person pointing — mouse, XR controller or pinched hand — behind one interface, and the
hover / press / drag / release machine that turns a stream of samples into an interaction.

### A pointer is three things

A ray, a select value in `0..1`, and whether it exists at all ([`PointerState`](graphics.md#pointing-pointer-kt-pointerstate)). That is enough to
unify every pointing device Field can see:

 - **A mouse** has a ray only because a camera can be inverted (`mousePointer`), a select value
   that is `0` or `1`, and is always active while the window has a cursor.
 - **An XR controller** has a pose and a trigger, and reports `active` when the runtime is tracking
   it (`controllerPointer`).
 - **A pinched hand** has 26 joints and a geometric pinch strength, read off
   [`afield.graphics.vulkan.targets.OpenXRHmdTarget`](graphics.md#openxrhmdtarget-kt-openxrhmdtarget)'s `handState`. Its select value is continuous and noisy,
   which is what the second half of this file is about (`pinchPointer`).

### Hysteresis, in two places

Feed raw nearest-hit results to a UI and it flickers. There are two flickers here and
[`PointerInteraction`](graphics.md#pointing-pointer-kt-pointerinteraction) treats them separately:

 1. **The part flickers** when the ray lands near an edge two parts share, or grazes a silhouette.
   A pixel's worth of hand tremor alternates the answer every frame, and a label that alternates
   every frame is unreadable. The fix is a **dwell** guarding every transition *away* from a held
   hover — see `PointerInteraction.switchSamples` and the rule stated on `resolveHover`. Acquiring
   a hover is never delayed, because a lag between pointing at something and it lighting up reads
   as the pointer being broken.
 2. **The click flickers** when a continuous select value sits on the threshold — which a
   geometric `pinchStrength` derived from a 40 mm range of finger separation does constantly. The
   fix is a **Schmitt trigger**: press at `PointerInteraction.pressThreshold`, release at the lower
   `PointerInteraction.releaseThreshold`. A value wobbling between them holds its state.

And once pressed, **the drag belongs to what it grabbed**: hover is frozen, and
`PointerInteraction.dragOffset` reports where the ray now crosses the plane through the original
contact point, so letting the pointer wander off the object does not drop the drag.

### Typical use

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
val scene = pickScene { add("model", mesh, parts = builder.groups()) }
val pointer = mousePointer(camera = { view.rayCamera(mesh) }, cursor = { window.cursor },
                           selecting = { window.isMouseButtonPressed(GLFW_MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT) })
val interaction = PointerInteraction(scene)
forever {
    interaction.update(pointer.sample())
    if (interaction.justPressed) println("grabbed ${interaction.grabbed?.partName}")
}
```

canvas's FLine coordinates. Lengths, speed and the pressure profile are the world's, measured along the line in 3D at `mmPerWorld` mm to a world unit: each sample carries its world arc (`TimedGesture.Sample.s`), so the two eyes' gestures press, pause and run out at the same places along the line however foreshortened each sees it. Each subpath is one movement of the hand (`gap` seconds apart); straight segments are sampled every `spacing` world units, curves finely enough to follow. The handle's `tilt`, `lean` and `roll` are as in `gesture`, its heading taken on this canvas. |

| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">prime</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">color</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec4</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">hiding</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.85</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">microns</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">60.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">stiff</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.4</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">texture</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.3</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">absorbent</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PaintCanvas</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintCanvas/#L787) | Lay a ground over the whole canvas: `microns` µm of `color` at `hiding`, with body `stiff` (fluid chalk-glue ≈ 0.2, oil lead white ≈ 0.6), roughened by `texture` before it levels. Dries the canvas first. `absorbent` (0..1, engine 4) makes it a chalk and glue ground that draws oil out of the paint laid on it — up to 0.6 coats' worth — so that paint dries leaner, stiffer and matte, until paint seals it. |

Fitted to the ground's thickness, so it reads best on an oil ground. Dries the canvas first. |

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">PaintNoise</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintNoise/#L12)

Smooth noise for varying a stroke along itself (`PaintCanvas.stroke`'s varied behaviours): a value from -1 to 1 that wanders as a stroke goes. Keyed on how far along a movement in the world a sample is (`TimedGesture.Sample.s`, mm), it lies at the same places along that movement on both canvases of a stereo pair, however long each sees it.

### LoadPart { #painttools-kt-loadpart }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">LoadPart</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">side</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">share</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">streak</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">seed</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintTools/#L106)

Which part of a brush a dip reaches (`PaintBrush.load`): a painter double-loads a brush by dipping one edge in a second pile.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">side</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | The edge of the brush's wide axis that goes in: -1 one edge, 1 the other, 0 the whole width alike. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">share</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | The share of the width, from that edge, that reaches the paint. |

By default they follow from the brush as it is (how full it is), so a restored brush dips alike; give a seed to fix them, as two eyes of a stereo pair must. |

### PaintLight { #painttools-kt-paintlight }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">PaintLight</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">azimuth</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">135.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">elevation</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">25.0</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">strength</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.0</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintTools/#L125)

A light to look at the canvas under (`PaintCanvas.render` `light =`): from `azimuth` degrees (0 from the right, 90 from the top, 135 the upper left) at `elevation` degrees above the canvas. Relief casts shadows along it, and wet paint has an oily sheen. `strength` scales the shading.

### PaintKnife { #painttools-kt-paintknife }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">PaintKnife</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">handle</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MemorySegment</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PaintTool</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintTools/#L329)

A painting knife: a flexible steel blade `width` canvas units long, and the bead of paint it carries. It lays paint in flat slabs with ridges where it is pressed out at the blade's ends and a bead where it lifts; pressed hard without paint it scrapes the wet paint off down to the dry surface. On engine 5 a slab tears where it parts from the blade. Get one from `PaintCanvas.knife`.

### PaintRag { #painttools-kt-paintrag }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">PaintRag</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">handle</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MemorySegment</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PaintTool</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintTools/#L373)

A soft cotton rag bunched into a pad `width` canvas units across, wiped or pressed over open paint to lift it (`PaintCanvas.wipe`, `PaintCanvas.blot`). What it lifts soaks into the cloth: the face in use loads up and lifts less until it is refolded (`PaintCanvas.refold`); dampened with spirits (`PaintCanvas.dampen`) it lifts nearly to the ground. Only wet paint comes away: past its gel point paint is part of the dry picture.

### WaterBrush { #painttools-kt-waterbrush }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">WaterBrush</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">handle</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MemorySegment</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PaintTool</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintTools/#L394)

A round watercolour brush: a belly that holds water, and the pigment dissolved in it. Where it touches the paper water flows between them by capillary suction, from the wetter to the drier: a full brush lays water and pigment, a damp one on a wet wash drinks it back up (with the pigment floating in it). A fast stroke lays less than a slow one. A light, nearly dry brush reaches only the peaks of the paper's tooth: drybrush comes from the paper, not a texture. Get one from `PaintCanvas.waterBrush`.

### DynamicBrush { #painttools-kt-dynamicbrush }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">DynamicBrush</span> <span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">constructor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">handle</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">MemorySegment</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">kind</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">BrushKind</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PaintTool</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/PaintTools/#L437)

A brush whose hairs move: a few dozen guide hairs simulated as chains of segments under a timed gesture of the handle ([`TimedGesture`](graphics.md#timedgesture-kt-timedgesture): position, pressure, tilt, lean and roll). The hairs bend against the paper and its paint, stick and slip by friction, clump when wet, and keep a bend they were forced past (retained deformation, so a brush once splayed stays splayed for a while). Load it with oil (`load`: upstream's bristles, following the hairs, carry and lay the paint) or with watercolour (`loadWater`). Get one from `PaintCanvas.dynamicBrush`.

## TimedGesture.kt { #timedgesture-kt }

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/paint/TimedGesture.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/TimedGesture/)

### TimedGesture { #timedgesture-kt-timedgesture }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">TimedGesture</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">samples</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Sample</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/TimedGesture/#L15)

A movement of the hand in time: where the tool is, when, how hard it presses, and how the handle is held. An [`afield.geometry.path.FLine`](graphics.md#fline-kt-fline) gives only a path; flicking, dragging slowly, pausing, pressing and lifting need the time and the orientation too. `PaintCanvas.gesture` makes one from an FLine at a speed; a pen or an agent can give the samples themselves.

## WaterMedia.kt { #watermedia-kt }

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/paint/WaterMedia.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/WaterMedia/)

**Used in:** [Watercolour and ink](../watercolor.md), [Brushes with moving hairs](../paint_gestures.md)

### Paper { #watermedia-kt-paper }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">enum</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">Paper</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">internal</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">id</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/WaterMedia/#L13)

A sheet of paper for watercolour and ink (`PaintCanvas.paper`). Each is a physical make-up — how much water it holds, how fast it drinks and wicks, its grain, tooth and sizing — not a texture: the same drop behaves differently on each because the water does. The numbers are estimates in the ranges reported for each kind of paper.

Constants: `ColdPress`, `HotPress`, `Rough`, `Xuan`, `Blotting`.

### WaterPigment { #watermedia-kt-waterpigment }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">WaterPigment</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">name</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">k</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">List</span><span class="p">&lt;</span><span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">&gt;</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">s</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">density</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">diameterUm</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">stain</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">lift</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/paint/WaterMedia/#L40)

A pigment as water carries it: its optics (Kubelka–Munk absorption `k` per channel and scattering `s`, per µg/mm² of pigment) and what decides how it moves — particle `density` (g/cm³) and `diameterUm` (dense, coarse pigment settles out onto the paper within a minute; fine pigment stays suspended), `stain` (per second it adsorbs onto fibres from water in the sheet, after which it can't be lifted) and `lift` (per second a deposit goes back into still water standing on it; a moving brush lifts much faster).

### TriangleCluster { #clustergeometry-kt-trianglecluster }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">TriangleCluster</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">firstVertex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">firstIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">vertexCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">triangleCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">clusterId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">geometryId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/ClusterGeometry/#L25)

One Field cluster description, eight uint32 words / 32 bytes, usable by ordinary compute shaders. Positions are vec4 (xyz in world/object units); indices are uint32 LOCAL to this cluster's vertex slice. A cluster may change counts, positions and indices on every build. IDs stay yours. Invalid GPU records become degenerate geometry and set `ClusterGeometry.status` rather than passing unchecked addresses/counts to Vulkan. No host readback occurs during builds.

### ClusterGeometryInput { #clustergeometry-kt-clustergeometryinput }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ClusterGeometryInput</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">positions</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">VulkanBuffer</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">indices</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">VulkanBuffer</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">clusters</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">VulkanBuffer</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/ClusterGeometry/#L38)

Borrowed producer buffers. Keep alive through build completion; synchronize any subsequent writes. `clusters` contains [`TriangleCluster`](graphics.md#clustergeometry-kt-trianglecluster) records. Buffer sizes, not arbitrary user-supplied addresses, determine bounds in the GPU validation/conversion pass.

### ClusterGeometry { #clustergeometry-kt-clustergeometry }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ClusterGeometry</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Renderer</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">capacity</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">verticesPerCluster</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">128</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">trianglesPerCluster</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">128</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">maxGeometryId</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AccelerationStructureAddress</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/ClusterGeometry/#L46)

General NV Mega Geometry builder: Field compute -> validated clusters -> CLAS -> one cluster BLAS. It owns bounded build/storage/scratch resources, never producer buffers. Single graphics queue; call `build` explicitly after a producer changes geometry. Static geometry needs only one build. Recreate to increase capacity. A rebuild changes this BLAS's bounds: rebuild the containing TLAS. Cluster BLAS has an address but no VkAccelerationStructure handle; use it in [`RayTracingInstance`](graphics.md#accelerationstructure-kt-raytracinginstance).

| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">onCreated</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/ModuleRebuild/#L60) | Called when a module has just made its uniform structures, before anything has written them. A uniform buffer starts as whatever memory it was given, so a member that must read as zero until set — a `stack.auto` numbers block's `foo_live` — is written here. |

## StandardDrawing.kt { #standarddrawing-kt }

The small vocabulary of `FLine` construction and styling that sketches and examples reach for
first.

`fline` is the builder; the `rangeTo` operator makes a one-segment line out of two vectors
(`a..b`, composable with `+=`), and the styling overloads of `moveTo` / `lineTo` / `cubicTo`
position a node and style it in the same call. Appearance is carried by delegated properties on
`FLine` and `FLine.Node` — `color`, `thickness`, `thicken`, `filled`, `stroked`, `pointed`,
`pointSize` — which the renderers read back; `onClick` and `hoverColor` only do anything in the
interactive outputs.

The rest are shape helpers: `rect` and `Rect.toFLine`, `arrow` (a real filled arrowhead rather
than a point sprite), `seg`, and `fitInto`, which scales and centres a list of lines into a
`Rect` using their 2D bounds only.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/)

**Used in:** [FLine examples (Field graphics)](../fline_examples.md), [Points into structure — Voronoi, Apollonius, contours and clusters](../spatial_geometry_examples.md), [Three.js scenes with `three { … }`](../three_output.md)

### Top-level values { #standarddrawing-kt-values }

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">color</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vector4f</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L124) | The line's colour as RGBA in `0..1` (sRGB, alpha included) — one colour for the stroke, the fill and the node dots alike. Opaque white when never set. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">color</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vector4f</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L135) | Per-node colour override in `0..1`, which is how one FLine carries a gradient: the GPU point/triangle writers in `afield.graphics.render.StandardDrawing` use a node's own colour where it has one and the whole line's `color` where it does not. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">thickness</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L141) | Stroke width, in the same units as the line's own points (pixels, for the 2D outputs). `null` — the default — means "unset", which every renderer reads as 1.0 rather than as "invisible". |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">thicken</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Stroke</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L151) | An AWT `Stroke` that replaces "stroke at one width" with "convert this line into the outline of its own stroke" — dashes, tapers, calligraphic pens, anything `Stroke.createStrokedShape` can do. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">filled</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L157) | Whether closed subpaths are flooded with `color`. `false` by default, and independent of `stroked` — with both true the renderers fill and then draw the outline on top. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">stroked</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L164) | Whether the path is stroked at `thickness`. `true` by default; with this and `filled` both false the geometry still exists and still hit-tests, but nothing is drawn except the node dots that `pointed` asks for. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">pointed</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L171) | Draw a dot at every node of the line — every `moveTo`/`lineTo`/`cubicTo` endpoint, not the interior control points of a cubic and not `close`. Off by default. The fast way to see where a path's points actually landed, and how a particle set gets drawn at all. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">pointSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L180) | Size of the dots `pointed` draws, 1.0 by default, overridable node by node with `FLine.Node.pointSize`. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">Node</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">pointSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L187) | Per-node override of the line's `FLine.pointSize`, under the same `* 3` radius convention. `null` — the default, and unlike the line-level property this one is not written back on read — means "follow the line". |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">onClick</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="nc">FLineIntersection</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">-</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L312) | Callback invoked when this FLine is clicked in an interactive output. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">label</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L321) | A human name for this line, reported back as `FLineIntersection.label` when it is clicked and used as the heading by `afield.ui.visualization.inspect`. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="nc">FLine</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="n">hoverColor</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec4</span><span class="o">?</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L327) | Color to show when the pointer hovers over this FLine in an interactive SVG output. When null no hover color change is applied. |

### FLineHitKind { #standarddrawing-kt-flinehitkind }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">enum</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">FLineHitKind</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L197)

What kind of thing on a figure a click landed on — the same three-way distinction the editable FLine widget already draws its hit targets with (`data-fline-hit-kind` in `sliders.js`), now reported to `FLine.onClick` as well.

Constants: `POINT`, `EDGE`, `FACE`, `UNKNOWN`.

### FLineFaceCoordinates { #standarddrawing-kt-flinefacecoordinates }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">enum</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">FLineFaceCoordinates</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L215)

Which convention `FLineIntersection.u` and `v` follow for a `FLineHitKind.FACE` hit — because there is no one right answer for a face nobody chose, and a plausible wrong number is worse than a labelled one.

Constants: `NONE`, `BILINEAR`, `BOUNDING_BOX`.

class="kc">null</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/StandardDrawing/#L247)

Hit information passed to `FLine.onClick` from the interactive line renderers — what a click on a figure *returns*.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">closestVertexIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Index into the line's `nodes` of the node nearest the click, or `-1` when the client did not work one out. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">position</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec3</span></code> | Where the click landed, in the line's own coordinate space. The three.js output fills in all three components; the 2D SVG output leaves `z` at 0 — `onElement` is the one to read for a depth, because it interpolates `z` along the element that was hit. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">kind</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FLineHitKind</span></code> | Which kind of element was hit. `FLineHitKind.UNKNOWN` when the output does not distinguish. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">lineIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Index of the clicked line within the lines passed to that one `lines(...)` call, or `-1` when unknown. The point of it: one shared `onClick` closure can serve a whole figure, instead of one closure per part. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">label</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | The clicked line's `FLine.label`, if it had one. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">nodeIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Index into the line's `nodes` of the node that *is* this element: the node itself for a `FLineHitKind.POINT`, the node that draws the segment for an `FLineHitKind.EDGE`, the `Close` for a `FLineHitKind.FACE`. `-1` when unknown. Unlike `closestVertexIndex` this is the element, not the nearest dot. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">subPathIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Which subpath (`moveTo`-delimited piece) of the line the element belongs to, or `-1`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">elementIndex</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Ordinal of the element among its own kind within the line — edge 0, 1, 2…; face 0, 1… Or `-1`. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">u</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span></code> | Where on the element the click landed, `0..1`, or `NaN` when it does not apply. |

Always `FLineFaceCoordinates.NONE` for a non-face hit. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">onElement</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Vec3</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | The point *on* the element nearest the click, in the line's own coordinate space, or `null`. |

Raster surface contract. XYZ world position + Vulkan depth [0,1] (clear=1, not reversed); XYZ world shading normal; linear RGB albedo. Motion is currentUV-previousUV, Y down, unjittered. Point sampling only. Material identity, emission, eligibility and temporal validity are NOT alpha. The optional RTXDI bridge snapshots these inputs; material IDs are not encoded in alpha.

### OpaqueRayScene { #opaquerayscene-kt-opaquerayscene }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">OpaqueRayScene</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Renderer</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">HasAccelerationStructure</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/lighting/OpaqueRayScene/#L41)

Static BLAS per geometry identity; a new TLAS for each explicit instance edit. No refit is claimed. Commit on the render thread between frames. Builds submit on Field's graphics queue and wait for their fence; removed resources retire via Field's frames-in-flight queue. This intentionally conservative first slice makes edits safe, at the cost of a stall on instance/topology edits.

## megaTextures.kt { #megatextures-kt }

A directory of images as one texture, however many of them there are.

`Box.megaTextureHere` is the whole box-facing surface: point it at a folder and it scans the
folder, builds the atlas, and registers the GLSL your shaders interpolate with `{{ mega.all }}`.
The machinery behind it lives in `afield.graphics.texture.mega`, and the reason it is worth reaching
for rather than a pile of `LoadedTexture`s is that it is *GPU-driven*: the fragment shader
measures its own on-screen footprint and asks for the resolution it needs, so nothing here has to
be told where anything is or how big it looks.

`dev_docs/agents/transcripts/mega_texture_wall.yaml` is the worked example — five lines of Kotlin
and two shaders you can edit live.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/render/megaTextures.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/megaTextures/)

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">OpenDlssNrPass</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Renderer</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">width</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">height</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/render/neural/OpenDlssNrPass/#L49)

Optional native Vulkan pass, recorded outside render passes on Field's graphics queue. Construct/evaluate/edit/close on the renderer thread. Recreate at a new resolution; close retires behind Field's completion fences. The output is linear RGBA16F, ready for normal Field grading. No CPU frame transfer or private per-frame submit occurs. Failure is explicit; callers can use availability() before creating the pass and present the source when unavailable.

### CompressedSplatPly { #compressedsplatply-kt-compressedsplatply }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">CompressedSplatPly</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/scene/CompressedSplatPly/#L42)

The PlayCanvas *compressed PLY* — the `.compressed.ply` that [splat-transform](https://github.com/playcanvas/splat-transform) writes and that SuperSplat and the PlayCanvas engine read back.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">const</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">CHUNK&#95;SIZE</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/scene/CompressedSplatPly/#L45) | Splats per chunk. Fixed by the format, not a tunable. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">const</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">SH&#95;C0</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/scene/CompressedSplatPly/#L48) | The DC term of the real spherical-harmonic basis, as 3DGS and splat-transform use it. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">const</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="nc">OPACITY&#95;LOGIT&#95;LIMIT</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/scene/CompressedSplatPly/#L58) | Opacity is stored as an 8-bit *sigmoid* value, so 0 and 255 invert to a logit of -infinity and +infinity. The uncompressed PLY column this reader emits is the logit, and callers downstream push it back through a sigmoid — an infinity there is either a NaN or, in [`GaussianSplatRenderer`](renderers.md#gaussiansplatrenderer-kt-gaussiansplatrenderer)'s case, a non-finite guard that lands on 0.5 and turns a solid splat translucent. Clamping to ±30 costs nothing: `sigmoid(30f)` is 1 and `sigmoid(-30f)` is 9.4e-14, both of which round-trip to the byte they came from. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">requiredChunkProperties</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/scene/CompressedSplatPly/#L61) | Chunk properties that every compressed PLY has, in the order the format declares them. |

## MeshFromDisk.kt { #meshfromdisk-kt }

The two missing edges between the loaders that read geometry off disk and the CPU renderer that can
*look* at it.

Field has four things that read geometry from a file, and until this file, one of them fed the CPU
preview:

 - `afield.geometry.mesh.mesh_io.kt` reads OBJ and STL straight into [`TriMesh`](graphics.md#mesh-kt-trimesh) — the type
   `afield.geometry.mesh.showMesh`, `TriMesh.renderPng` and the inline `toHTML()` card all render.
 - [`PlySupport`](graphics.md#simpleplysupport-kt-plysupport) reads PLY (ASCII, binary, both endians, colours, normals, point clouds) into a
   packed 10-float GPU buffer.
 - [`GltfSupport`](graphics.md#simplegltfsupport-kt-gltfsupport) reads glTF/GLB — and, being `Assimp.aiImportFile` underneath, also FBX, DAE, 3DS,
   OBJ, STL and PLY — into a packed 12-float GPU buffer plus materials.
 - `afield.graphics.scene.fabricated.FabricateGltfBridge` takes that same model into the PBR `StandardRenderer`.

Both GPU loaders produce plain host memory — `memAlloc`, not a Vulkan allocation — so nothing
except a missing function stopped their output from becoming a [`TriMesh`](graphics.md#mesh-kt-trimesh). These are those
functions: `PlySupport.PlyModel.toTriMesh`, `assimpToTriMesh` and the dispatcher
`meshFromAnyFile`, plus a `Box.showMesh` overload that takes a `File`.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
showMesh(File("/path/to/thing.glb"))                     // straight to the orbitable viewer
val m = meshFromAnyFile("/path/to/scan.ply")             // or keep the mesh and compute with it
println(m.summary())
```

They live here rather than in `afield.stdlib` on purpose: `mesh_io.kt` is deliberately
dependency-free, and these need LWJGL. `afield.graphics.scene.*` is in every box's default imports
(see `afield.document.graph.intro`), so a box can call them without an import anyway.

What is *not* here, because nothing in the tree can read it: **STEP / IGES / BREP**. There is no CAD
kernel on the classpath, and a NURBS-to-mesh tessellation is not a weekend's work — see
`public/docs/geometry_from_disk.md` for the full list of what does and does not load.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/scene/MeshFromDisk.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/scene/MeshFromDisk/)

**Used in:** [Geometry from disk](../geometry_from_disk.md)

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/shader/learning/GpuShaderTraining.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/shader/learning/GpuShaderTraining/)

### GpuShaderTraining { #gpushadertraining-kt-gpushadertraining }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">GpuShaderTraining</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Renderer</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">width</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">height</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">batchSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">256</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">seed</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="mi">42</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/shader/learning/GpuShaderTraining/#L36)

A small reusable learned RGB function, trained directly from Field images on the graphics queue. Architecture matches LearnedShader: 16 positional features -> 32 ReLU -> 32 ReLU -> RGB. Slang differentiates the network; cooperative-vector outer products accumulate its gradients. FP32 Adam master weights/moments, loss-scaled FP16 gradients and inference matrices. The source remains caller-owned. Train/evaluate/close only between or within render-thread work. No CPU image/weight readback is used in train/evaluate. This is not a general graph ML runtime.

## shaders.kt { #shaders-kt }

The bridge between a box's text and a live Vulkan pipeline: shader source lives in box
properties, and this file turns it into modules and keeps them hot-reloading.

The properties come first — `vertex`, `fragment`, `compute`, `task`/`mesh`, the ray-tracing
stages, and a `_s` variant of each for Slang — alongside `once.vertex { }`-style seeders. The
user-facing entry points are the macro placeholders `Box.moduleHere`, `Box.computeModuleHere`,
`Box.meshModuleHere`, `Box.rayTracingModuleHere` and `Box.shadertoyHere`; each one throws
`MacroNotExpandedException` if actually called, because `MacroRegistry` is expected to rewrite it
into the real `_moduleHere`-family call.

Before compilation every stage goes through `preprocess`, which resolves `{% property %}` template
tags against other boxes' shader properties (with cycle detection and `#line` fixups) and against
built-in includes such as the field probe, field stats and quantile warp. Registered include roots —
`registerShaderFilesystemIncludeRoot` for a directory, `registerLygiaIncludeRoot` /
`shaderCachedUrlIncludeRootResolver` for URL-fetched, disk-cached libraries — are **not** reachable
from here: they are resolved by shaderc during compilation, from a real `#include` only. It also expands
`{% copyPC %}` (copying a previous stage's push-constant block) and stackAuto template slots
compiled from StackSL via `stackAutoShaderSource`.

`reloadShader`, `reloadComputeShader`, `reloadMeshShader` and `reloadRayTracingShader` are the
reload path: compile, report errors back onto the box's source lines, introspect the result, and
rewrite the box's Kotlin preamble with generated binding structures before swapping the module.
`Box.attachShader` adopts an externally built module into that same path. `Box.fieldProbeHere`,
`Box.fieldStatsHere` and `Box.fieldProbeAutoControl` attach the GPU readback instrumentation.

Everything here needs a live `Box` — properties, error reporting, preamble edits and the
generation-guarded async reload all key off it.

Only `RELATIVE` includes are resolved relative to `requestingSourcePath`'s directory. |
| <code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">includeDepth</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code> | How deep this include is nested, straight from shaderc. Informational — nothing in Field enforces a limit on it. |

## typography.kt { #typography-kt }

Text as geometry: a string becomes contours, and from there everything Field already does to
geometry applies to letters.

A layout here is a value you can extrude, march, sample or animate, not a label painted into a
raster — which is what every other use of `java.awt.Font` in the tree does (`MeshGallery`,
`ImagingGallery`, `montage`'s 5x7 bitmap font). It needs no dependency beyond AWT:
`Font.createGlyphVector(...).getOutline()` hands back real quadratic/cubic glyph outlines, and it
works headless. `typography_field.kt` is the bridge to Field's own 2D and 3D outputs.

### The three values

 - [`Typeface`](graphics.md#typography-kt-typeface) — a font at a size, from a logical/system name (`typeface`) or a `.ttf`/`.otf` on
   disk (`typefaceFromFile`). Carries the vertical metrics (ascent, descent, leading) a layout
   needs.
 - [`Glyph`](graphics.md#typography-kt-glyph) — one glyph's outline, cached per typeface and glyph code, in its own frame with its
   origin on its own baseline. Both representations live side by side: `Glyph.contours` are
   flattened, nesting-classified, winding-normalised polygons for geometry work, and
   `Glyph.outline` is the same rings as an [`FLine`](graphics.md#fline-kt-fline) of *real cubics* for drawing.
 - [`TextLayout`](graphics.md#typography-kt-textlayout) — glyphs placed on baselines by AWT's own advances and kerning, plus tracking,
   multi-line and alignment. Every glyph in it is a [`PlacedGlyph`](graphics.md#typography-kt-placedglyph) carrying **mutable transform
   handles** (offset, rotation, scale, pivot). Those handles are how you animate letters
   individually, and `TextLayout.onCurve` is nothing but a routine that sets them from an
   [`FLine`](graphics.md#fline-kt-fline)'s arc length.

### Text space

Glyph and layout coordinates are **x right, y down**, origin at the first baseline, units = the
typeface's size in points. That is AWT's own glyph frame and it is also the frame Field's 2D
outputs use (`Rect`'s y grows downwards), so text handed straight to `Box.lines` or
`Box.showText` reads the right way up with no transform. The 3D bridges in `typography_field.kt`
flip y at their own boundary, because a mesh wants y up.

### The winding convention

A glyph's counter — the hole in `o`, `e`, `a`, `B` — is only a hole if something says so, and what
the font shipped is not enough to go on. (`isoContourFLines` in `contours.kt` leaves winding
arbitrary, and every consumer downstream has to cope.) So this file *decides*:

> For a ring `p0..pn`, signed area is `½Σ(xᵢyᵢ₊₁ − xᵢ₊₁yᵢ)` in text space. **Outer contours are
> positive; holes are negative.** A ring's `GlyphContour.depth` — how many other rings of the same
> glyph contain it — is authoritative: even depth is an outer contour, odd depth is a hole. A ring
> whose area sign disagrees with its depth is *reversed* on the way out.

Both representations obey it, so `contours.filter { it.isHole }` and the subpaths of
`Glyph.outline` agree, and `TypographyTest` asserts it on glyphs whose answer is known by eye
(`o` has one hole, `l` has none, `%` has two).

### AWT and the main run loop

`imaging_field.kt:417` explains why `montage` captions with a bitmap table instead of
`Graphics2D.drawString`: on macOS, touching the AWT font manager pulls in AppKit, which competes
with GLFW for the main run loop, and `Server.main` never initialises the toolkit. This
family cannot avoid the font manager — it *is* the font manager — so it contains the hazard in one
place, `Typefaces.warm`, whose KDoc carries the measured stack trace and the conclusion:

> **A JVM that wants glyph outlines and passes `-XstartOnFirstThread` must also pass
> `-Djava.awt.headless=true`.** Otherwise `CFontManager.loadFonts` dispatches to the process's first
> thread and waits forever for a run loop nobody is pumping.

`Typefaces.warm` detects that in four seconds and throws with that sentence in it, rather than
hanging the editor. Every jvm-main gallery in the tree already sets the property in the first line
of `main`, `jvmTest` does not need it (Gradle's test JVM has no `-XstartOnFirstThread`), and an
interactive Field window pumps its run loop through `glfwPollEvents` and so is expected to be
fine — expected, not tested; see `Typefaces.warm`. Everything after that one touch is pure
computation over cached outlines.

## typography_field.kt { #typography-field-kt }

The bridges out of a [`TextLayout`](graphics.md#typography-kt-textlayout) and into the four families Field already has.

`typography.kt` answers with *structure* — rings, depths, advances, handles — and structure is not
yet a drawing, a mesh, an image or a point cloud. This file is the missing hop, and it is the
reason the typography family is worth having at all: once a string is contours, letters get to be
inputs to machinery that never knew about text.

It is the typographic counterpart of `spatial_field.kt` (plane geometry → `FLine`) and
`mesh_field.kt` (`TriMesh` → `FLine`), and it is written to the same rule: every function here
returns a *value* — no `Box`, no output — except the two figure helpers at the bottom, which are
`drawToSVG` and so work headless, in a test and in the docs build.

Five bridges:

 1. **→ [`FLine`](graphics.md#fline-kt-fline)** (`TextLayout.toFLines`, `TextLayout.toFLine`, `Glyph.toFLine`). One line per
    glyph, so a per-glyph handle actually moves something, with the font's real cubics intact.
    Filling works because of `typography.kt`'s winding convention and nothing else: Skia and
    Java2D both fill non-zero, so a counter is a hole precisely because its ring runs the other
    way. `TextLayout.toFLines` takes `honourHoles = false` to show you the blob you get without a
    convention, which is the control arm the docs figure uses.
 2. **→ [`TriMesh`](graphics.md#mesh-kt-trimesh)** (`TextLayout.toMesh`). Hole-aware extrusion: `extrudeMesh` in
    `mesh_generate.kt:619` and `triangulatePolygon` (`:547`) explicitly cannot do holes, so the
    caps here go through `FloatEarcut` with hole indices and the walls are emitted ring by ring
    from the *same* flattened vertices, which is what makes the result watertight — and makes an
    extruded `o` genus 1 and an extruded `l` genus 0.
 3. **→ an SDF** (`TextLayout.toSdf`). A 2D signed-distance grid, bilinearly sampled and extruded
    in z, so letters compose with `sdfSphere`, `sdfSmoothUnion`, `.twisted()` and everything else
    in `mesh_sdf.kt`, and `marchingCubes` will mesh the result.
 4. **→ [`Img`](imaging.md#imaging-kt-img)** (`rasterizeText`). An analytic even-odd scanline fill of the layout's own rings —
    *not* `Graphics2D.drawString`, both because AWT text rendering in-process is what
    `imaging_field.kt:417` forbids and because filling our own outlines means a legible PNG is
    evidence about *this* code rather than about AWT's rasteriser.
 5. **→ points** (`TextLayout.samplePoints`, `TextLayout.toPointFLine`). Even-by-arc-length
    samples along the outlines, which is what the alife agents, the clusterers and the
    contourers in `clustering.kt` / `alife_agents.kt` consume.

Frames: bridges 1, 3, 4 and 5 stay in text space (y **down**, origin on the first baseline);
bridge 2 flips y at its boundary, because a mesh wants y up, and re-normalises winding when it
does.

Requires `ImageData.exportOpaqueFd` = true at creation. Per the spec each call to vkGetMemoryFdKHR transfers ownership of a *new* fd to the caller, so this caches and returns the same fd on repeated calls — call `close` to release it, don't just drop the value. The fd stays valid (and open in this JVM process) for the streamer's whole session; the helper process only ever gets a *duplicate* via /proc/<pid>/fd/<fd> (see WIRE_FORMAT.md's Linux addendum), never this one. |

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">data</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">DmaBufPlaneLayout</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">offset</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">rowPitch</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/texture/LinuxDmaBufExport/#L30)

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/texture/UnixFdPass.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/texture/UnixFdPass/)

### UnixFdPass { #unixfdpass-kt-unixfdpass }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">UnixFdPass</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/texture/UnixFdPass/#L36)

Sends raw file descriptors to another process via SCM_RIGHTS over a Unix domain socket — the mechanism [`VulkanExternalMemory`](graphics.md#vulkanexternalmemory-kt-vulkanexternalmemory)'s `field-encode-linux` handoff actually needs.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">available</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/texture/UnixFdPass/#L38) | The optional helper must be built before starting an external-memory session. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">closeFd</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">fd</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/texture/UnixFdPass/#L62) | Close an owned export descriptor after SCM_RIGHTS duplicated it, or on setup failure. |
| [<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">sendFds</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">socketPath</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">fds</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">IntArray</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/texture/UnixFdPass/#L74) | Connect to the AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM socket at `socketPath` (a peer must already be listening — see `field-encode-linux`'s Linux `open` handling) and send every fd in `fds` in one `sendmsg` call (one SCM_RIGHTS control message, fds preserved in array order). Returns false on any failure (socket missing/not listening yet, connect refused, send failed) — callers should retry with backoff for the "not listening yet" race rather than fail immediately. |

### VideoDecoder { #videodecoder-kt-videodecoder }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">VideoDecoder</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">videoPath</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">String</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">outputFormat</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">VideoDecodeFormat</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">VideoDecodeFormat</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">P010</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/texture/video/VideoDecoder/#L26)

VideoDecoder wraps FFmpeg functionality to decode video frames. Converts decoded frames either to P010 for ordinary video display or to tightly-packed RGBA8 for data-bearing RGB movies. The latter matters for atlases whose R/G/B channels are values rather than colour: routing those through 4:2:0 YUV would irreversibly subsample the channels.

### VideoFrame { #videodecoder-kt-videoframe }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">VideoFrame</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">width</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">height</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">format</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">VideoDecodeFormat</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">plane0</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ByteBuffer</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">plane1</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">ByteBuffer</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">plane0Stride</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">plane1Stride</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">timestamp</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">release</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Unit</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">{</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">AutoCloseable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/texture/video/VideoDecoder/#L417)

A decoded upload frame. P010 uses both planes; RGBA8 uses `plane0` and leaves `plane1` empty. The owner must `close` the frame after upload or when superseding it so its large backing buffers can be reused without waiting for garbage collection.

VideoTexture manages video playback with P010 format support. Maintains configurable texture slot arrays for luma and chroma planes in semi-planar format. Supports load, play, scrub, and unload operations while reusing Vulkan resources when dimensions match.

relative to one render origin. Boolean geometry is never read back from these Float buffers. Lines follow geometric creases and open boundaries within each part; coplanar construction boundaries and triangulation diagonals are omitted. Separate parts retain their edges. Z-up is an optional rigid display rotation (x,z,-y); canonical data and artifact identity stay unchanged. An overlay uses the same part ID/group as its solid, so visibility and supplied motions agree. |

Presentation overrides for a named part. Colours are RGB values in 0..1. A null xrayOpacity follows the viewer slider; 1 keeps an important part opaque. These settings do not change geometry, picking, assembly groups or review identity.

## VisionGeometryPreviewBox.kt { #visiongeometrypreviewbox-kt }

The in-Field half of [`VisionGeometryPreview`](graphics.md#visiongeometrypreview-kt-visiongeometrypreview): turning "my mesh only exists in the headset" into a
picture in the box you wrote it in.

A Live Metal box's Kotlin never runs on the Mac — it compiles to JavaScript for the head — so its
output panel is normally empty of anything but log lines. `Box.previewVisionGeometry` fills that
gap: it takes the box's own source, runs it for real (see `VisionGeometryPreview.capture`) and
draws the resulting mesh straight into the box's output. One command, and your headset geometry is
on the desktop.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/graphics/visionos/VisionGeometryPreviewBox.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/visionos/VisionGeometryPreviewBox/)

Immutable: [`VisionPoseStream`](graphics.md#visionpose-kt-visionposestream) republishes a whole new frame rather than mutating the last one, so a renderer that captured `VisionPoseStream.latest` at the top of its frame keeps a consistent head and eyes all the way through it — the association between a pose and the image drawn from it is the whole point of the milestone.

### VertexBuffer { #vbuffer-kt-vertexbuffer }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">VertexBuffer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Renderer</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">size</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">usage</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">VK10</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="nc">VK&#95;BUFFER&#95;USAGE&#95;VERTEX&#95;BUFFER&#95;BIT</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">createCPU</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">HasBuffer</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="nc">BufferWriteable</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/buffers/VBuffer/#L22)

this is, as far as I can tell, completely decoy — with resizable BAR (or unified memory on Apple Silicon) this staging buffer thing is just excess engineering _and_ writing shaders that do their own pulling is better _and_ device pointers set through push constants is faster and architecturally skips all of the descriptor nonsense

### ImageLayouts { #imagelayouts-kt-imagelayouts }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">ImageLayouts</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/device/ImageLayouts/#L23)

`VK_KHR_unified_image_layouts`: with it, `GENERAL` is as good as any specialised layout for every use, so a driver that offers it has nothing to gain from Field's per-use layouts, and a layered driver such as KosmicKrisp has work to lose (a transition it must honour for Metal).

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">BinocularGazeIntersection</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">minimumAngleDegrees</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.25</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">maximumSeparation</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.03</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">minimumDistance</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.05</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">maximumDistance</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Double</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">8.0</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/BinocularGazeIntersection/#L18)

Closest approach of two forward eye rays, in metres, with explicit rejection of unreliable depth. Real rays can be skew: `position` is the midpoint of `leftPoint` and `rightPoint`, and `separation` is their gap. Read `valid` before placing an object there.

### MotionItems { #motionitems-kt-motionitems }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">MotionItems</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/MotionItems/#L27)

Correspondence by stable item identity, not draw-list index. Call `begin` once per rendered frame (duplicate calls are harmless). Topology or material changes use a different revision; camera cuts and world resets call `clear`. Retains only this frame and its immediate predecessor. Owner-thread only.

### EyeGazeState { #openxreyetracking-kt-eyegazestate }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">EyeGazeState</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/OpenXREyeTracking/#L14)

Combined gaze from `XR_EXT_eye_gaze_interaction`, in the target's LOCAL reference space (metres, +Y up, -Z forward). Updated in place on the renderer's queue thread. Numeric pose values retain the last valid observation; check `poseValid` before using them.

### HtcEyeTrackingState { #openxreyetracking-kt-htceyetrackingstate }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">HtcEyeTrackingState</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/OpenXREyeTracking/#L108)

HTC per-eye gaze, pupil and geometry observations, updated in place on the renderer's queue thread. The three streams have independent validity and OpenXR timestamps (nanoseconds). A failed stream does not suppress the other streams. Numeric values retain the last valid observation; timestamps reset to zero when a query fails or a frame is skipped.

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">open</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">PingPongRenderToTexture</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Renderer</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">fromContext</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">frameCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">parameters</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RTTParameters</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Unit</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">{</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RenderToTexture</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">parameters</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/PingPongRenderToTexture/#L47)

RenderToTexture variant that ring-buffers every color attachment. Each frame it renders into one image set while exposing previous completed frames via `otherImageView` and `previousFrameImageViews`, so modules can sample feedback history without managing several RTT instances.

### FrameCadencedPingPongRenderToTexture { #pingpongrendertotexture-kt-framecadencedpingpongrendertotexture }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">FrameCadencedPingPongRenderToTexture</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Renderer</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nf">fromContext</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">framesPerPingPong</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">frameCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">parameters</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">RTTParameters</span><span class="p">.</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="o">-&gt;</span> <span class="nc">Unit</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">{</span><span class="p">}</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">PingPongRenderToTexture</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">frameCount</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">parameters</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/PingPongRenderToTexture/#L646)

A [`PingPongRenderToTexture`](graphics.md#pingpongrendertotexture-kt-pingpongrendertotexture) that only advances the frame ring once every `framesPerPingPong` render calls. Between advances, `thisImageView` remains the latest completed texture and `otherImageView` remains the previous one, so downstream modules can crossfade from `other` to `this` with `crossfade`.

### RendersAfter { #rendertarget-kt-rendersafter }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">interface</span> <span class="nc">RendersAfter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/RenderTarget/#L331)

A pass that has to render after another [`Target`](graphics.md#renderer-kt-target) in the same list: a publisher after the texture it publishes. Wherever it was added, [`RenderTarget`](graphics.md#rendertarget-kt-rendertarget) moves it behind `rendersAfter` before it iterates.

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RollingCapture</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">renderer</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Renderer</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">source</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Image</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">rowsPerFrame</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">16</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">sourceLayout</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">VK&#95;IMAGE&#95;LAYOUT&#95;SHADER&#95;READ&#95;ONLY&#95;OPTIMAL</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">private</span> <span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">downsample</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">)</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/graphics/vulkan/targets/RollingCapture/#L35)

Rolling capture that copies a horizontal strip from a source image into an internal snapshot image each frame. Once a full frame has been copied, you can copy the snapshot to a CPU-visible buffer (e.g., on a low-priority transfer queue) without stalling rendering.

A uniform spatial grid over a buffer of particles, built on the GPU every frame, so a compute shader can ask "who is near me" without looking at everybody.

Other applications list it under Field's app name and this `name`. |

Waits up to `waitMs` for it to appear, then throws, listing the servers it could see. Reuses the open client cached under exactly `match`; a missing or closed client is recreated. Calls with different matches have separate cache slots. Clients persist across box runs; close one explicitly when its shared connection is no longer needed. |

### Syphon { #syphon-kt-syphon }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">object</span> <span class="nc">Syphon</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/io/syphon/Syphon/#L41)

Field's end of [Syphon](https://syphon.info), the macOS standard for sharing GPU frames between applications: a [`SyphonServer`](graphics.md#syphon-kt-syphonserver) publishes frames that Resolume, TouchDesigner, MadMapper, OBS (with its Syphon source), VDMX or Max can receive, and a [`SyphonClient`](graphics.md#syphon-kt-syphonclient) receives what they publish.

## SolidAgreement.kt { #solidagreement-kt }

The measurement this package exists for: **one written shape, evaluated two completely independent
ways, and the disagreement reported as a number.**

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
val bracket = cuboid(4, 3, 1) - cylinder(2, 0.5).at(1, 0, 0)
println(bracket.crossCheck(SolidQuality(edgeLength = 0.02, segments = 256)).report())
```

### Two implementations that share no code

Almost nothing in a graphics codebase gets to do this. The usual options are to assert against a
remembered constant (which pins the current behaviour, not the correct one) or against a closed
form (which only exists for a handful of shapes). Here both sides are *implementations*, and they
share no code whatsoever:

| | side A | side B |
|---|---|---|
| the shape becomes | a distance field over `Double`s | a CSG tree over Manifold handles |
| the surface comes from | `afield.geometry.mesh.marchingCubes`, in Kotlin | Manifold's exact boolean kernel, in C++ |
| the volume comes from | a sum of signed tetrahedra over `Float` triangles | Manifold's own integration, in `double` |
| the genus comes from | edge/vertex adjacency in `mesh_topology.kt` | Manifold's Euler characteristic |

There is no path by which a bug in one produces the same wrong answer in the other. Five-figure
agreement is therefore strong evidence that both are right, in a way that any number of assertions
against constants would not be.

The same argument has since been applied to a **third** reading — the differentiable one in
`SolidGradient.kt`, which is `toScalarField`'s arithmetic replaced by
[`afield.math.autodiff.AD`](math.md#autodiff-kt-ad) and shares no line of code with it. It is measured by
`SolidExpr.gradientAgreement` rather than folded in here, and the reason is that the two compare
different objects: this file compares **surfaces** — volume, area, genus, Hausdorff deviation —
and the differentiable reading produces a *field*, exactly as `toScalarField` does. Folding it in
would have meant inventing a volume for something that has none. What the two share is the
argument, so each cross-references the other.

### Agreement does not converge to zero

There are two regimes:

 - **Polyhedral shapes** — cuboids, polygon-profile extrusions, and booleans of those. The exact
   lowering *is* the truth, so the marched one converges to it and the residual goes to zero as
   `SolidQuality.edgeLength` shrinks. Expect the relative volume error to fall roughly as `h²`.
 - **Curved shapes** — anything with a sphere, a cylinder, a circular profile or a round offset.
   Manifold's circle is an **inscribed n-gon**, whose area falls short of the true one by
   `1 − (n/2π)·sin(2π/n) ≈ 2π²/3n²`. The field lowering describes the true curve. So agreement
   converges to that deficit and not to zero, however fine the march.

`facetingDeficit` computes the second one from the segment count alone, so a curved shape's
residual can be checked against a *predicted* floor rather than a remembered one. That is the
difference between "these two numbers are close" and "these two numbers are as close as the
geometry permits, and here is the formula".

## SolidExact.kt { #solidexact-kt }

Lowering **(b)**: a [`SolidExpr`](graphics.md#solidexpr-kt-solidexpr) as an *exact* Manifold [`Solid`](graphics.md#solid-kt-solid) — or a stated refusal.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
when (val l = (cuboid(2, 2, 1) - cylinder(3, 0.3)).exactSolid()) {
    is SolidLowering.Lowered -> println("volume ${l.value.volume}, genus ${l.value.genus}")
    is SolidLowering.Refused -> println("no exact form: ${l.why}")
}
```

### Refusals are in the type

The discipline is [`afield.lang.rectsl.RectSLFnLowering`](languages.md#rectslfn-kt-rectslfnlowering)'s, wholesale, and for the same reason it gives:
a wrong answer is worse than no answer, so the lowering never guesses. Every node either maps to
the corresponding Manifold call or refuses **with a reason**, and the refusal propagates up.

A `null` would invite a caller to substitute something plausible; a thrown exception loses the
reason at the first `runCatching`. A stated reason survives into a test assertion, a diagnostic and
a docs page — which is why the refusals in this package are enumerable and enumerated:

| node | why there is no exact form | flavour |
|---|---|---|
| `SolidExpr.SmoothUnion` | the fillet surface lies on **neither** operand, so no sequence of unions, intersections and differences of the two can produce it | permanent |
| `SolidExpr.SmoothDifference` | the same, for the filleted cut | permanent |
| `SolidExpr.Gyroid` | a trigonometric field on all of space, not a bounded volume | permanent |
| `SolidExpr.Round` | `minkowskiSum` with a sphere exists, but that sphere is an inscribed polyhedron, so the result is strictly *inside* the true offset by up to its sagitta — and refining the march does not close a gap that is not the march's | *would not converge* |
| `SolidExpr.Shell` | `grow − erode` exists as two Minkowski operations, with `SolidExpr.Round`'s problem twice over and a concave decomposition between them | *would not converge* |

The last two are the interesting ones. They are not "we did not get to it": an exact-looking answer
is available and is **the wrong answer**, systematically and in a direction that does not shrink.
Filing them beside the smooth blends would flatten a real distinction, so the type carries
`SolidLowering.Refused.closable` and the reason says which kind it is.

Note what is **not** on the list. Every [`Profile`](graphics.md#solidexpr-kt-profile) node lowers exactly — including `Profile.Offset`,
because `Section.offset(d, JoinType.ROUND)` is definitionally the Minkowski sum with a disc, which
is *exactly* what `sdf − d` means. So a rounded slot has an exact form and a rounded solid does not,
and the asymmetry is real: Clipper offsets a 2D region as a region, where the 3D story has to go
through a polyhedral ball.

### SolidExpr { #solidexpr-kt-solidexpr }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">sealed</span> <span class="k">interface</span> <span class="nc">SolidExpr</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/lang/solidsl/SolidExpr/#L88)

A 3D solid written down as a **value** instead of as a closure — the symbolic notation that `afield.geometry.mesh`'s signed-distance family and `afield.geometry.solid.manifold`'s exact CSG kernel can *both* evaluate.

## SolidField.kt { #solidfield-kt }

Lowering **(a)**: a [`SolidExpr`](graphics.md#solidexpr-kt-solidexpr) as a signed distance field, so everything `mesh_sdf.kt`,
`marchingCubes` and `Solid.levelSetOf` already do keeps working unchanged.

```diffstatic {data-lang=kotlin}
val mesh = (cuboid(2, 2, 1) - cylinder(3, 0.3)).march(resolution = 96)
```

### This lowering always succeeds

Unlike `exactSolid`, this lowering always succeeds. Every node in the algebra has a field form —
that is where the algebra came from. What it does *not* always have is an **exact** distance
function, and the difference matters to a ray marcher (which steps by the field's value and
overshoots if the value is an overestimate) even though it does not matter to a marching cubes
(which only reads signs). `fieldNotes` enumerates the places where the field is sign-correct but
not metric-correct, so the gap is a fact rather than a surprise.

### It is thread-safe, deliberately unlike the `sdf…` family

`mesh_sdf.kt` is explicit that a [`ScalarField3D`](graphics.md#mesh-sdf-kt-scalarfield3d) "must **read** the vector it is handed and not
write to it", and its own combinators capture a single scratch `Vec3` to transform into. That makes
them fast and single-threaded.

This lowering does not do that. Internally it builds a tree of [`Field3`](graphics.md#solidfield-kt-field3) — a `fun interface` over
three primitive `Double`s, so there is no boxing and nothing to alias — and only wraps a `Vec3` at
the very top, in `toScalarField`. So the field is re-entrant and safe to call from any thread.
